settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Your library's profile, locations, borrowing rules, policies and integrations.

nav.label: Settings sections
nav.system_link: Jobs, schedules and health are on the System page

sub.profile: How your library introduces itself in the public catalogue and in notices.
sub.branches: Library locations. Items, patrons, budgets and pickups are tied to a branch.
sub.item_types: Physical formats, whether they can be reserved, and what a lost copy costs.
sub.categories: Borrower types with their own limits, membership period and fine block.
sub.rules: Loan periods, renewals and fines for every patron category and item type.
sub.policies: Circulation, catalogue, privacy and sign-in policies for the whole library.
sub.notices: How overdue, hold and courtesy notices reach patrons.
sub.integrations: AI features and the services connected to your library.
sub.audit: Every change, sign-in and job, newest first.
sub.maintenance: Run maintenance tasks, import records and patrons, and export the catalogue.

denied.title: Administrator access required
denied.body: Your account can't change library settings. Ask a library administrator if something needs changing.
denied.section: Your account doesn't have permission to open this section.

identity.title: Identity
identity.desc: Shown in the catalogue header, page titles and every notice.

opac.title: Public catalogue
opac.desc: What patrons can do themselves in the online catalogue.

circulation.title: Borrowing
circulation.desc: Renewals and fines applied at the desk and by the nightly run.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.desc: How long the library keeps borrowing history linked to a patron.

cataloguing.title: Cataloguing
cataloguing.desc: Automatic help while records are edited.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.desc: Retries for notices that could not be delivered.

ai.title: AI features
ai.desc: Turn the AI assistants on or off for staff and the public.

channels.title: Delivery channels
channels.desc: Configured by your system administrator on the server.

connected.title: Connected services
connected.desc: Sign-in providers, self-check machines and catalogue exchange.

library_name.label: Library name
library_name.help: Shown in the catalogue header, browser tabs and notices.

opac_announcement.label: Catalogue announcement
opac_announcement.help: A banner at the top of every public page — opening hours, closures, events. Leave empty to hide it.

allow_patron_self_renewal.label: Patrons can renew online
allow_patron_self_renewal.help: Patrons may renew their own loans from their account, within the circulation rules.

auto_renew_when_no_holds.label: Automatic renewal
auto_renew_when_no_holds.help: The nightly run renews loans that nobody else is waiting for.

fines_skip_closed_days.label: No fines on closed days
fines_skip_closed_days.help: Overdue fines count only the days the issuing branch is open, using the library calendar.

allow_self_registration.label: Online card registration
allow_self_registration.help: Visitors may apply for a library card online; staff approve each application.

self_registration_category.label: Category for new registrations
self_registration_category.help: The patron category given to people who register online.

allow_purchase_suggestions.label: Purchase suggestions
allow_purchase_suggestions.help: Patrons may suggest titles for the library to buy.

allow_reviews.label: Ratings and reviews
allow_reviews.help: Patrons may rate and review titles in the catalogue.

reviews_require_approval.label: Approve reviews before publishing
reviews_require_approval.help: New reviews stay hidden until a staff member approves them.

anonymize_history_after_days.label: Anonymise loan history after
anonymize_history_after_days.help: Returned loans older than this are detached from the patron. 0 keeps history forever.

require_2fa_for_staff.label: Require two-factor sign-in for staff
require_2fa_for_staff.help: Staff must set up an authenticator app at their next sign-in.

lockout_threshold.label: Lock accounts after failed sign-ins
lockout_threshold.help: Failed attempts before an account is temporarily locked. 0 never locks.

lockout_minutes.label: Lockout duration
lockout_minutes.help: How long a locked account stays locked.

session_idle_timeout_minutes.label: Sign out idle sessions after
session_idle_timeout_minutes.help: Inactive sessions end after this long. 0 keeps them until they expire.

notify_new_signin.label: Alert on sign-in from a new device
notify_new_signin.help: Send the account holder a notice when they sign in from a new device or network.

password_reset_enabled.label: Self-service password reset
password_reset_enabled.help: Allow “Forgot password?” resets by email from the sign-in page.

authority_auto_link.label: Link headings to authorities automatically
authority_auto_link.help: When a record is saved, link its names and subjects to authority records and use the authorised form.

notice_max_attempts.label: Delivery attempts per notice
notice_max_attempts.help: How many times a notice is retried before it is marked as failed.

ai_assistant_enabled.label: Staff AI copilot
ai_assistant_enabled.help: Show the AI assistant to staff (Ctrl + J).

ai_opac_enabled.label: AI search in the public catalogue
ai_opac_enabled.help: Allow natural-language search and recommendations for patrons.

settings.key_hint: Setting key (used by the API and the command line)
settings.announcement_placeholder: e.g. The library is closed on Monday for maintenance.
settings.in_use: “{name}” is still in use, so it can't be deleted. Move what uses it first.

channels.console: Not sending — written to the server log
channels.note: Channels are set with server environment variables (LIBROWISE_EMAIL_BACKEND, LIBROWISE_SMS_BACKEND). Message wording is edited under Notices.

integrations.public_url_unset: Not set — links use the address of each request
integrations.sso_desc: Let staff and patrons sign in with your organisation's accounts.
integrations.sip_desc: Accounts for kiosks, security gates and e-book platforms.
integrations.copycat_desc: Remote catalogues searched when cataloguing new titles.
integrations.endpoints_desc: SRU, OAI-PMH and linked-data addresses to share.

f.code_help: Short unique code, e.g. MAIN. Capital letters, digits and _ only.
f.code_pattern: Use capital letters A–Z, digits and underscores only.
f.code_taken: Another entry already uses this code.

branches.empty_body: Add your first library location. Items, patrons and pickups are tied to a branch.
branches.delete_text: “{name}” will be removed permanently. A branch that still has items, patrons or rules can't be deleted.

item_types.empty_body: Item types describe formats such as books, DVDs or journals.
item_types.delete_text: “{name}” will be removed permanently. Item types that are still used by items or rules can't be deleted.
item_types.holdable_help: Turn off for reference or short-loan material that can't be reserved.
item_types.cost_help: Charged when an item of this type is declared lost.

categories.empty_body: Categories group borrowers — adults, children, staff — with their own limits.
categories.delete_text: “{name}” will be removed permanently. Categories that patrons or rules still use can't be deleted.
categories.membership_help: How long a new or renewed card stays valid.
categories.block_help: Patrons owing this much or more can't borrow until they pay.

rules.precedence: The most specific rule wins: an item-type rule beats a patron-category rule, which beats a branch rule.
rules.matrix_caption: Effective circulation rules at {branch}: patron categories by item types
rules.matrix_help: Arrow keys move between cells; Enter opens a cell to create, edit or delete its rule.

source.explicit: Set by a rule for this exact combination.
source.default: No rule matches; built-in defaults apply.

rules.empty_body: Without rules, every loan uses the built-in defaults (14 days, 2 renewals).

f.loan_days_help: Days until the item is due.
f.max_renewals_help: How many times the loan can be renewed.
f.grace_days_help: Days after the due date before fines start.
f.fine_cap_help: Overdue fines on one loan never exceed this.
f.hold_pickup_days_help: Days a held item waits on the shelf.

panel.title: {category} · {item_type}
panel.new_sub: Choose what it applies to, then set the values.
panel.explicit: This combination has its own rule (#{id}). Changes apply to new loans.
panel.inherited: This combination currently follows the rule for {rule}. Saving creates a rule just for this combination.
panel.default: No rule matches this combination, so built-in defaults apply. Saving creates a rule for it.
panel.exists: A rule for this combination already exists — open it from the matrix to edit it.

rules.delete_text: The rule for {rule} will be deleted. Loans it covered will follow the next broader rule.

explain.title: Explain a rule
explain.desc: Pick a branch, patron and item type to see which rule a loan would use — and why.
explain.summary: {category} patrons borrowing {item_type} at {branch} keep it for {days} with up to {renewals}. Overdue fines are {fine} a day, capped at {cap} per loan.
explain.why: When several rules match, the most specific one wins.
explain.none: No rule matches this combination, so the built-in defaults apply.

audit.caption: Audit events, newest first
audit.empty_body: Try a different person, action or date range, or clear the filters.

maint.system_title: Background jobs, schedules and system health
maint.system_body: The job queue, schedules, workers, database and backups are on the System page.
maint.nightly_confirm: This sends due notices to patrons, expires uncollected holds and may renew loans. It normally runs on its own every night.
maint.marc_desc: Add bibliographic records with their holdings from another library system.
maint.marc_help: MARC21 (.mrc) or MARCXML, up to 50 MB. Titles already in the catalogue (same ISBN) are skipped; 952 holdings become items.
maint.patrons_desc: Bring in borrowers from a CSV file, such as a Koha patron export.
maint.patrons_help: Existing card numbers are skipped. Unknown category or branch codes use the first one defined.
maint.export_desc: Download every record with its holdings — for backups or moving to another system.

roles.title: Roles & permissions
roles.subtitle: Who can do what: custom staff roles, staff accounts, per-person access and single sign-on.
roles.denied_body: Managing roles and staff accounts needs the “Manage staff accounts” permission. Ask a library administrator.
roles.roles_intro: Custom roles add permissions on top of a person's built-in role — for example a circulation-desk role for a student assistant.

builtin_desc.patron: Library members: the public catalogue and their own account.
builtin_desc.librarian: Front-line staff: circulation, cataloguing, patrons, acquisitions and reports.
builtin_desc.admin: Everything, including settings, security and permissions added later.

roles.everything: Administrators hold every permission, including ones added by future modules.
roles.empty_body: Create a role to delegate specific duties without making someone an administrator.

delete_text.one: {count} account loses the permissions this role grants and is signed out. Type the role name to confirm.
delete_text.other: {count} accounts lose the permissions this role grants and are signed out. Type the role name to confirm.

roles.additive_note: Permissions are added to the person's built-in role. You can only grant permissions you hold yourself.
roles.cannot_grant: You don't hold this permission, so you can't grant it.
roles.staff_intro: Everyone with staff access. Built-in roles are changed on the patron record; custom roles can be assigned here.
roles.find_help: Type at least two characters, then choose a person from the list.
roles.pick_body: Search above by name, card number or email to see exactly what that person can do, where each permission comes from, and their sign-in security.

effective_n.one: {count} permission, and where it comes from.
effective_n.other: {count} permissions, and where each comes from.

roles.history_desc: The latest 100 sign-in attempts for this account.

confirm.mfa_text: Their authenticator and recovery codes are removed and every session ends. They must set up two-factor again.
confirm.sessions_text: Every browser and device signed in as this person is signed out immediately.
confirm.tokens_text: Scripts and integrations using these tokens stop working. Revoked tokens can't be restored.
confirm.unlock_text: The failed-attempt counter is cleared and they can sign in again straight away.

sso.intro: Let staff and patrons sign in with an OpenID Connect provider such as Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace or Keycloak. Accounts are matched by linked identity, then by verified email.
sso.id_taken: A provider with this ID already exists.
sso.empty_body: Add your organisation's identity provider so people can sign in with their existing account.
sso.delete_text: People who sign in with this provider will need a password instead. Type the provider ID to confirm.

f.id_help: Lowercase letters, digits, - or _. Used in the callback URL and can't be changed later.
f.label: Button label
f.issuer_help: Settings are read from the issuer's /.well-known/openid-configuration document.
f.secret_keep: Stored encrypted. Leave empty to keep the current secret.
f.domains_help: Comma-separated. Leave empty to accept any verified email.
f.auto_create_help: First-time sign-ins become new patron records.

perm.opac: Use the public catalogue and manage their own account
perm.catalog_read: View the staff catalogue, items and lookup tables
perm.catalog_write: Create and edit records and items
perm.circulation: Check out, check in, renew, receive transfers and take payments
perm.circulation_override: Override circulation blocks (limits, fines, expiry, renewals)
perm.holds_manage: Place, cancel and manage holds for patrons
perm.fines_charge: Add manual charges to patron accounts
perm.patrons_manage_staff: Manage staff accounts, custom roles and their access
perm.acquisitions_write: Create vendors, budgets and orders; receive orders
perm.notices_manage: Manage notice templates and the message queue
perm.settings_manage: Change settings, security policy and single sign-on
perm.admin: Administer lookup tables, imports and maintenance
perm.calendar_manage: Edit the library calendar (closed days and holidays)
perm.notices_outbox: View the notice outbox and resend notices
perm.serials_write: Create subscriptions, receive and claim issues
perm.courses_write: Manage courses and put items on reserve
perm.interop_manage: Manage SIP2 accounts and copy-cataloguing targets
perm.kiosks_manage: Set up and manage self-checkout kiosks
perm.authorities_write: Create, edit, merge and delete authority records
perm.labels: Print spine labels, item barcodes and library cards

system.title: System
system.subtitle: Health, background jobs, schedules, workers, database and backups.
system.denied: The System page needs the “Run and schedule background jobs” permission.
system.run_intro: The job is queued straight away; a running worker picks it up within seconds.
system.cancel_text: The job is removed from the queue and won't run. You can retry it later.
system.no_jobs_body: Nothing in the queue with these filters. Scheduled jobs appear here when they run.
system.schedules_desc: Recurring jobs started by the scheduler.
system.tz_note: Schedules run on {tz} time; times here are in your time zone.
system.no_schedules_body: Recurring jobs are configured with the LIBROWISE_SCHEDULES setting.
system.no_workers_body: Start one with: python -m librowise worker --concurrency 2
system.latency_desc: This server process, since it started.
system.no_latency_body: Figures appear once the server has handled some requests.
system.backups_note: Backups are made by the backup job or from the command line and can never be downloaded through the web. Restore from the command line on the server.
system.no_backups_body: Run the “Database backup” job, or schedule it, to create one.

interop.title: Interoperability
interop.subtitle: Self-check terminals over SIP2, remote catalogues for copy cataloguing, and the standard addresses other systems use to reach your catalogue.
interop.read_only: Only administrators can change SIP2 accounts and copy-cataloguing targets. You can still read the configuration and the endpoint reference.

sip.intro: Each self-check kiosk, security gate, sorter or e-book platform signs in with its own account.
sip.login_taken: Another account already uses this login.
sip.delimiter_rule: Use a punctuation character such as |.
sip.delete_text: Terminals using this login can no longer connect. Consider disabling the account instead. Type the login to confirm.
sip.empty_body: Create one for each self-check kiosk, gate or e-book platform.
sip.readonly_title: SIP2 accounts are managed by administrators
sip.readonly_body: Ask an administrator to add or change a terminal account. How to run the SIP2 server is shown below.
sip.run_desc: The SIP2 server is a separate process. Run it next to the web server and point terminals at its address and port.
sip.tls_note: SIP2 sends card numbers and PINs in plain text: keep it on the library network or a VPN, or start it with --certfile and --keyfile for TLS.
sip.bins_help: Codes sent back to automated sorters (field CL) for returned items.

f.login_help: Letters, digits and . _ @ - (the terminal's CN field).
f.password_help: At least 10 characters mixing letters, digits and symbols (the CO field).
f.password_keep: Leave empty to keep the current password.
f.name: Terminal name
f.branch_help: Loans and returns are recorded at this branch.
f.networks_help: Comma-separated addresses or ranges (CIDR). Empty allows any address.
f.checked_in_ok: Accept returns of items not on loan
f.checked_in_ok_help: Useful for book drops and sorters.
f.checksums_help: AY/AZ error detection on every message.
f.idle_help: Disconnect terminals that stay silent this long.

targets.intro: Remote SRU catalogues searched when cataloguing new titles. Records are fetched as MARCXML.
targets.builtin_note: The built-in Library of Congress catalogue is in use. Once you add a target, only the targets listed here are offered.

test_ok.one: {name} answered in {ms} ms ({count} match for a sample search).
test_ok.other: {name} answered in {ms} ms ({count} matches for a sample search).

targets.delete_text: Cataloguers will no longer be able to search this catalogue. Type its name to confirm.
targets.empty_body: Add a remote catalogue that supports SRU.
targets.denied_body: Copy-cataloguing targets are visible to cataloguers only.
targets.indexes_help: CQL index names this server uses for title, author and ISBN searches.

f.name: Name
f.url_help: The address that answers SRU searchRetrieve requests.
f.enabled_help: Disabled targets are hidden from cataloguers.

ep.intro: Share these addresses with partner libraries, union catalogues, discovery services and self-check vendors.
ep.sru_desc: Search/Retrieve via URL with CQL queries, in MARCXML or Dublin Core. Used by other libraries' copy cataloguing, discovery layers and reference managers.
ep.oai_desc: Metadata harvesting for union catalogues, aggregators and discovery services: oai_dc and marc21, one set per material type, deletions reported.
ep.ld_desc: Every public record page embeds schema.org JSON-LD (book, author, ISBN, date, language, availability per branch) and Open Graph tags, so search engines and link previews understand it.
ep.sip_desc: 3M Standard Interchange Protocol 2.00 over TCP for self-check kiosks, security gates, sorters and e-book platforms. Default port 6001, | as field delimiter.
